_note: Notes about the work. A note with "body" is published here first (its own page plus feed.xml, which other sites import with a link back). A note with "home" was first published elsewhere and is only listed. Block types: p, h2, ul. Plain text only; no HTML. Links must be https to a known host (tools/notes.py).

posts.title: One home for my open work, and where else to find it
posts.summary: My open projects now have one home, Public Good Works. This note lists where else they appear, and which copy to trust.

body.p: My open projects on data and AI for UK public services, and my personal public-good projects, now have one home: Public Good Works, at cyberdudeuk.github.io. This note lists where else they appear, and which copy to trust.

ul: The launchpad lists every public project with its status, licence and live site.
The code is on GitHub, and each repository is preserved in the Software Heritage archive.
Most projects' releases have a citable DOI through Zenodo, linked to my ORCID record.
Notes like this one are written here first and copied to DEV, with a link back to this page as the original.

body.p: The launchpad is the source. It links to each of my profiles and each profile links back to it, so you can check they belong to the same person. If a copy elsewhere differs, the launchpad is the one kept current.
Use the contact form linked from the launchpad, or the one on each project's own site. There is no email route.
These are personal projects and personal views. None is an official government service, policy or endorsement unless the project says so.

posts.title: Making a portfolio of open public-sector projects that keeps itself honest
posts.summary: The routines that keep the project list accurate, and the one rule they all follow: they propose, and a person merges.
